file-catalog-with-saved-data-01.graded_text: Saved data is reached through the same read, write, exact-edit, and delete-file tools used for source files and assets, as file paths such as JSON files. The catalog has no separate tools for records, entries, collections, or the database.

votes.e: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:5 "Agents build static sites by editing files and maintain live saved data through separate entry tools. Saved data is never a file"; the catalog defines separate `data_list`, `data_get`, `data_create`, `data_update`, `data_delete` tools (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:219-269) and a `collection` $def (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:26), so saved data is not reached through the file read/write/edit/delete tools.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-02.graded_text: No tool has a required idempotency key, revision or version token, or confirmation argument. Protection against stale writes is enforced by the server, for example by rejecting a write that would overwrite changes made since the agent's read and asking for a fresh read.

votes.e: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:56 "Every update/delete supplies `expectedRevision`." and B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:58 "Every mutation requires `requestId`."; every mutation schema lists them as required, e.g. `file_edit` B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:172 "required":["siteId","path","expectedRevision","replacements","requestId"] and `site_delete` B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:120 "required":["siteId","expectedRevision","requestId"]. Required idempotency keys and revision tokens are exactly what the assertion excludes.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-03.graded_text: The design explains how a visitor's write made after the agent read a saved-data file survives the agent's later write of that file: it is merged safely or the agent's write fails with a conflict. A plain last-writer-wins replacement does not pass.

votes.e: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:259 "The entry revision protects the entire entry, including nested fields. If a visitor writes anything between the read and commit, return `CONFLICT`, even when the changed fields differ. Reread, preserve the visitor's latest values, and reconsider the requested repair." plus B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:56 "A stale revision returns `CONFLICT` ... and changes nothing." A visitor write made after the agent's read makes the agent's write fail with a conflict, so it is not last-writer-wins. (The unit is an entry, not a file, but the conflict guarantee itself is spelled out.)

file-catalog-with-saved-data-04.graded_text: Deleting files takes an explicit nonempty list of exact paths, deleting a whole site is its own tool, and no omitted argument widens a deletion or makes an update create a new site.

votes.e: `file_delete` B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:179 "Delete exactly one existing file by canonical path and revision." with required `path` (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:182) and B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:185 "No recursive or prefix deletion."; whole-site deletion is the separate `site_delete` (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:115-123); B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:279 "No optional path or omitted entry ID can turn a narrow delete into a site-wide delete."; `file_update` B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:165 "Requires an existing path; never creates one implicitly." and no tool upserts a site (only `site_create` creates one). One exact path per call meets the nonempty, exact-target substance, though it is not a list. Closest omitted-widens case: `files_list` B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:135 "omitted or empty means all paths", but that is a read only.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-05.graded_text: Writing a saved-data file as a whole is checked entry by entry against the site's declared write rules and validation, with the agent holding only the rights of the person it acts for, so replacing the whole file cannot make a change that person could not make one entry at a time.

votes.e: There is no whole-file saved-data write to check entry by entry: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:217 "There is no whole-store get/set, reset, replace, import, or delete-by-filter tool." Also, agent writes are not limited to the site's declared rules: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:209 "Owners always retain administrative read/write capability." and B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:60 "Saved-data maintenance requires owner-equivalent permission". No site-declared validation is applied to agent writes at all; `value` is any object (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:30).

file-catalog-with-saved-data-06.graded_text: There is no separate tool or argument for setting a site's title, description, or favicon. They come from index.html.

votes.e: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:10 "Title, description, and favicon are derived from `index.html`. There are no parallel metadata setters."; `site_create` B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:113 "There is no title, description, favicon, template, or publishing mode argument."; `settings_get` B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:197 "It does not contain title, description, or favicon." I checked every input schema in B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md (lines 78-267): none has a title, description, or favicon property. `sites_list` only returns them read-only (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:91).

blocking: [claude] Saved data gets a second, parallel API instead of the file tools: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:5 "maintain live saved data through separate entry tools. Saved data is never a file". It adds five `data_*` tools plus `settings_get`/`settings_update` on top of the file tools (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:189-269). Agents must learn two mutation models, and an engineer building it ships the duplicated surface.

[claude] Stale-write safety and retry dedupe are pushed onto tokens the agent has to hold: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:56 "Every update/delete supplies `expectedRevision`" and B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:58 "Every mutation requires `requestId`", required even on `site_delete` (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:120) and `site_create` (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:110). An agent that loses the revision, or reuses a requestId on a different input, gets `REQUEST_ID_REUSED`/`CONFLICT` instead of the server detecting staleness from its own read record.

[claude] Agent writes bypass the site's declared write rules and validation: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:209 "Owners always retain administrative read/write capability" with `value` as an unconstrained object (B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:30). Nothing checks an agent's data write against the site's rules or validation, so an agent can store values or shapes that the site's own rules would reject from any person one entry at a time.

[claude] The design rewrites the runtime SDK contract, which is out of scope for an MCP catalog: B/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:259 "The browser SDK must also use revision-checked mutations, or an equivalent atomic field operation". With revision-checked SDK writes, concurrent visitors ticking the same shared checklist item (brief: "anyone may tick a shared checklist item") conflict with each other, and the 'or equivalent' leaves the choice uncommitted.
